facts.text: Mount Union sprang up in the late 19th century as a small agricultural hub near Cotton Grove, thanks to the railroad’s 1850s expansion.
The town sits close to the Skunk River, which shapes local drainage patterns across the prairie.
Early settlers were drawn to Mount Union’s fertile prairie lands, making it a prime spot for 19th‑century agriculture.
Main Street still showcases 19th‑century commercial buildings, including the Johnson Harness Shop and the historic Smith Drugstore and Ice Cream Parlor.
Mount Union once operated as an incorporated city with its own government, post office, schools, and businesses until residents chose unincorporation amid financial challenges.
